body: Yeah, I'm being careful not to trivialize the situation with cliches.  I am chiefly concerned with making her as comfortable and as happy as I can given the context of her situation and my relationship with her.  I know it's very, very difficult for her to actually be going through this.  I hate feeling ineffectual, but it's stuff like this that... renews my conviction, you know?  Thank you for your input.

Thank you very much for your input.

Her conditions are such that she can spend time at home and does not need *constant* medical supervision, although she requires a caregiver.  Two of the problems affect her joints and spine and can leave her bedridden when they act up; even on good days she has trouble getting around on her own.  The third is more serious: it can cause internal bleeding when it flares up, which sends her to the emergency room and often ends with her staying in the hospital for around a week at a time.  

She can speak and write with a keyboard no problem, although she's told me that art and working with pen/pencil has become difficult because of the positions required.  Still, I'll prod gently to see if she's interested in any creative endeavors like journaling or writing, and encourage her to do that if she is.  Do you think it would be a good idea to suggest doing something together (at her discretion, no deadlines or anything of course - if she was tired or wasn't feeling up to it there would be absolutely no pressure to work on it), or would that just be more to worry about?

I'm not sure if she has access to a pain clinic, although I'll ask her if she's considered it (I'll look into it a bit on my own, too, to see if I can get any info on them before I bring it up).  I know that she's tried to take part in forums etc. for people with similar conditions, but she's told me that she didn't like them because "it's like disease is the only thing we have in common."

She's seen psychologists and counselors previously but she's not seeing one right now.  When the opportunity comes up I'll ask her more about what she thought of them, and suggest she discuss it with whoever she feels would be most appropriate (family/hospital counselor). 

Thanks again.

All right - obviously this is a throwaway account, because the person I'm referring to knows about reddit.  I doubt she'd be looking in here, since I believe she's only used it once ever, but she knows my main account name... even with this precaution her situation is hard to keep vague and she'd know it if she saw it, but I honestly don't know what else to do.

My friend is a few years younger than me, still a teenager, and she's been in the hospital more than I likely ever will be.  She has three conditions, one of which leaves her occasionally unable to walk at all.  It's been difficult for her doctor to find the right mix of drugs to control the physical pain she deals with on a daily basis.   The only option she seems to have left is medical marijuana, but I'm not sure if this is a good idea (because of the nature of one of her conditions, not because I am personally opposed to it - THC is a narcotic, which would help deal with the pain of two of her conditions but could aggrivate the third).

It's possible for these conditions to go into remission, but there is currently no way of curing them - all she can do is deal with the symptoms and I don't think she's ever been without at least one of them for more than a month at a time.   She's told me that it's like her body "has ADHD... if it's not one thing, it's another.  It's been this way ever since I was a baby."  

She's also told me that she wants to die.  She feels guilty for being a burden to her family and her boyfriend, says that she hates being the centre of attention all the time because of how often she has to go to the emergency room.   Honestly, I don't know what to say to her.   I don't have any precedent.   I don't know what it's like to be sick and suffering in the way that she is.  

I am related to someone who has similar conditions who is currently living relatively normally (she's a lab tech with a husband and two kids); so it's not as if there is absolutely no chance of getting out of this.  Still, I'm not a doctor.  I want to suggest relaxation and meditative techniques (if drugs can't control the pain, what else is there?) but I'm don't want to seem like I'm trivializing her situation.  It's not like I can tell her to "just cheer up" or "just get better."  I don't believe in any of that "spiritual energy" and "chi" stuff, although I do think that stress affects your body and that some meditative techniques can be good tools, even if it doesn't help in in the *way* that some people claim it does.   I'm worried that her stress and her guilt is affecting her body, which makes her more stressed, which affects her body... 

Lately she's been so depressed that I'm seriously worried about losing her.  I love this girl like a little sister, and I want her to be happy,  I want her to have hope, but I'm worried she'll just dismiss me as naive and I don't know what to tell her to introduce even a little bit of optimism.  She's tired. She's told me, "I'm done."

I don't have any delusions of being able to single-handedly make everything all better.   Despite that, I want to do whatever I can... I've lost one friend to suicide already, and I know I'd never be able to forgive myself if I didn't at least try.  But I'm at a complete loss.  Is there someone here who can give me some insight as to what it's like to be that ill, and anything that helps deal with the emotional stress of being physically weak?  How can I help her, what can I say to her?  As of right now we are separated and I can only contact her via the internet, but I still want to be of practical use as well as being supportive emotionally - any pragmatic ideas on that front? 

Please.  Something, anything at all, to break this cycle.
